Lesson 1.3.1: Activities & Roles

10 Week English Program · Day 3 · Vocabulary · CEFR A2–B1 · 60 min

Lesson 1.3.1 Overview

Activities & Roles: Communicating Responsibilities and Solving Problems

Total Duration 60 Minutes

Welcome to Day 3! Use the familiar setting of a community BBQ to describe activities, assign responsibilities, explain problems, and coordinate solutions. Then transfer these communication skills to a BPO team setting. Move from A2 descriptions toward confident B1 interactions.

01. Vocabulary

Learn 12 transferable expressions for responsibilities, problem-solving, and customer communication.

02. Accuracy

Use accurate patterns with in charge of, assigned to, follow up on, and responsible for.

03. Communication

Coordinate roles, respond to unexpected problems, and communicate clear next steps in social and BPO workplace scenarios.

STEP 1 · ENCOUNTER

What Is Happening at the BBQ?

8 minutes

Look at all three pictures first. With a partner, describe what you see, identify activities and equipment, discuss who might be responsible, and predict possible problems.

Notice

What activities and equipment can you identify?

Assign

Who might be in charge of food, equipment, and safety?

Predict

What if the sound system stops working or refreshments run low?

Speaking frame

“I think ___ is in charge of ___. If ___ happens, we could ___.”

STEP 2 · CLARIFY

Vocabulary Lab: Activities and Roles

12 minutes

Study 12 expressions used in daily life and BPO. Flip each card to see its meaning and two examples: one at a BBQ and one at work.

Vocabulary Check · 12 Questions

Score: -/12
STEP 3 · REMEMBER

Match, Choose & Complete

10 minutes

Select the best answer for each real-life or workplace situation. Submit your answers to receive explanations.

Key Accuracy Rule

Use be in charge of / be responsible for + noun or -ing; be assigned to + base verb; follow up on + issue or request. Example: “Maya is in charge of the equipment. Alex is assigned to look into the issue.”

STEP 4 · INTERNALIZE

Dialogue Analysis: A Quick Team Huddle

10 minutes

Read or listen to a team huddle before a BBQ. Notice how teammates assign responsibilities, report unexpected issues, coordinate solutions, and promise updates.

Audio uses your browser's text-to-speech voices. The complete transcript is provided below.

Nina: The BBQ starts in twenty minutes. I'm in charge of the overall event, but I need to confirm everyone's roles.

Leo: I'm responsible for refreshments, and I've been assigned to handle the drink delivery.

Nina: Great. Did you run into any issues?

Leo: Yes. The delivery is late. I'll follow up on it with the supplier and keep you updated.

Nina: Thanks. Please coordinate with Maya, too. She's in charge of guest check-in.

Maya: I can take care of check-in, but I need someone to set up the sound system.

Nina: Sam was assigned to set it up. Unfortunately, the speakers aren't working. Sam, could you look into the problem?

Sam: Of course. I'll check the cables first and make sure the equipment is connected correctly.

Leo: While Sam investigates, I can handle guests' questions about the schedule.

Nina: Perfect. Let's confirm: Leo will follow up on refreshments and handle questions; Maya will take care of check-in; Sam will look into the speakers. I'll coordinate with everyone and keep the team updated.

Maya: Sounds good. If we run into another issue, we'll let you know right away.

Comprehension Check · 7 Questions

STEP 5 · INTERNALIZE

Who Handles What? · Role-play

15 minutes

Work with a partner. Choose one situation, discuss the problem, clarify responsibilities, and agree on next steps. Then switch roles and try the second situation.

Manual practice timer

03:00

Daily Life: Two Unexpected Problems

The BBQ starts in 20 minutes. The sound system has stopped working and the drinks delivery is late. One student is the event coordinator; the other is a volunteer.

Your mission

  1. Report both issues using “We ran into an issue with …”.
  2. Clarify who is in charge of equipment and refreshments.
  3. Coordinate two actions and agree on when to follow up.
  4. Confirm the plan and say how you will keep the team updated.

BPO Workplace: Training Room Setup

Your team is preparing a short training activity. The headset audio isn't working, and two participants need assistance. One student is the team lead; the other is a support agent.

Your mission

  1. Report the technical issue using “We ran into an issue with …”.
  2. Clarify who is responsible for checking the equipment.
  3. Offer to handle participants’ questions and look into the audio problem.
  4. Confirm next steps and promise a follow-up update.

Useful language

“I’m in charge of …” · “I’ve been assigned to …” · “We ran into an issue with …” · “Let me look into …” · “I’ll coordinate with …” · “I’ll follow up on …” · “I’ll keep you updated.”

STEP 6 · FLUENT USE

Final Challenge: The Coordination Huddle

5 minutes

Your BBQ team has five minutes before guests arrive. Deliver a concise update: who is responsible for what, what two problems appeared, what actions the team will take, and how everyone will receive updates. Use at least six of the 12 target expressions. Do not simply list items; communicate a workable plan.

1. Assign

Identify at least three responsibilities using in charge of / assigned to / responsible for.

2. Solve

Describe two problems using run into an issue, then offer to handle or look into each.

3. Confirm

Confirm next steps, including how and when you will follow up or keep everyone updated.

B1 stretch goal

Explain why you chose each action: “I’ll coordinate with Sam first because we need to fix the speakers before guests arrive.”
